origin.description: Lift nested data-frame columns into one frame.

arguments.name: recursive
arguments.text: Flatten nested frames inside nested frames.

origin.example:
x <- data.frame(driver = c("Bowser", "Peach"), occupation = c("Koopa", "Princess"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
x$vehicle <- data.frame(model = c("Piranha Prowler", "Royal Racer"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
x$vehicle$stats <- data.frame(speed = c(55, 34), weight = c(67, 24), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cat(paste(names(flatten(x)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: A nested frame's columns are prefixed with the parent name.

arguments.name: recursive
arguments.text: Flatten nested frames inside nested frames.

translation.details: recursive false keeps the inner frame as one column.
translation.example:
from jsonlite import DataFrame, flatten
vehicle = DataFrame({"model": ["Piranha Prowler", "Royal Racer"]})
vehicle.columns["stats"] = DataFrame({"speed": [55, 34], "weight": [67, 24]})
frame = DataFrame({"driver": ["Bowser", "Peach"], "occupation": ["Koopa", "Princess"], "vehicle": vehicle})
print(" ".join(flatten(frame).columns))
